chapterName: Early Rome & the Kingdom: The Foundation of an Empire (753-509 BCE)

questions.question: How did the reign of Tarquinius Priscus end after 38 years?
options: He was struck by lightning from Jupiter
He was murdered by a son of Ancus Marcius
He died in exile at Cumae
He fell in battle against the Sabines
He was killed by his daughter and her husband
questions.explanation: Tarquinius Priscus was murdered by a son of Ancus Marcius, the king who had adopted him. He is remembered for introducing the symbols of office and celebrating the first triumph.
questions.sourceQuote: After 38 years on the throne, he was murdered by a son of Ancus Marcius.

questions.question: Which items formed part of a Roman king's traditional dress? (select all that apply)
options: A purple robe embroidered with gold
A white band around his head
questions.explanation: The king wore a gold-embroidered purple robe, red shoes and a white band around his head, and he sat on a special chair. The historian Momigliano suggested the reality was rougher, with many kings really leading armed bands.
questions.sourceQuote: He sat on a special chair and wore a purple robe embroidered with gold, with red shoes and a white band around his head.

questions.question: Where and when did the exiled Tarquin the Proud die?
questions.explanation: Tarquin died in exile at Cumae, a Greek city near Naples, in 495 BC. His attempts to return had failed, ending with Rome's victory over a Latin alliance at Lake Regillus.
questions.sourceQuote: Tarquin died in exile at Cumae, a Greek city near Naples, in 495 BC.

questions.question: Around 730–720 BC, at about the time a wall was built on the Palatine, what happened to the Forum area?
options: It was walled off as an Etruscan fortress
Burials stopped and parts were paved as a shared space
A palace for Romulus was built over it
It was flooded and abandoned for a century
It became a royal burial ground for the kings
It was given over to chariot racing
questions.explanation: As the Palatine wall went up, burials in the Forum stopped and parts of it were paved over. It became a shared space for meeting and worship.
questions.sourceQuote: At about the same time, burials in the Forum stopped and parts of it were paved over, turning it into a shared meeting and worship space.

questions.question: Legend credits King Numa with adding which two months to create a twelve-month calendar?
questions.explanation: Numa was said to have added January and February to make a twelve-month calendar. Rome waited a year after Romulus vanished before choosing him as king.
questions.sourceQuote: Legend credits him with adding January and February to make a twelve-month calendar.

questions.question: According to tradition, which kinds of newcomers did Romulus welcome into his new city? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Romulus welcomed newcomers of every kind, including exiles, criminals and runaway slaves. He was also credited with creating Rome's basic institutions.
questions.sourceQuote: He welcomed newcomers of every kind, including exiles, criminals and runaway slaves.

questions.question: Which modern historian suggests that the Etruscan king Lars Porsenna may have ended Rome's monarchy himself?
questions.explanation: Tim Cornell put forward this idea. It builds on the Roman historians Tacitus and Pliny, who recorded that Porsenna actually captured Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: The historian Tim Cornell suggests that Porsenna may have ended the monarchy himself.

questions.question: Which of these achievements are credited to Servius Tullius? (select all that apply)
options: Building the Temple of Diana on the Aventine
Dividing the city into four districts by residence
questions.explanation: Servius divided Rome into four districts based on where people lived and built the Temple of Diana on the Aventine. Ostia and the first prison belong to Ancus Marcius, and the Circus Maximus to Tarquinius Priscus.
questions.sourceQuote: He also divided the city into four districts by where people lived, and he built the Temple of Diana on the Aventine Hill.

questions.question: Which hill people living south-east of Rome did Tarquin the Proud fight?
questions.explanation: Tarquin fought the Volsci, a hill people to the south-east. His wars made Rome the leading power among the Latin cities.
questions.sourceQuote: He fought Rome's neighbours, including the Volsci, a hill people to the south-east, and made Rome the leading power among the Latin cities.

questions.question: In the legend, what did Romulus and Remus do once grown, before setting out to found their own city?
options: Took the throne of Alba Longa for themselves
Served as priests of Mars in Alba Longa
Led the Latins against the Etruscans
Overthrew Amulius and restored their grandfather
Fled to Troy to find their ancestors
questions.explanation: The twins overthrew Amulius, who had seized Alba Longa's throne, and restored their grandfather Numitor. They then quarrelled while founding their city, and Remus was killed.
questions.sourceQuote: Grown up, the twins overthrew Amulius and restored their grandfather.
